Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

Nestimate 1.2.0

This version collects everything since 0.9.24, the last release on CRAN. Some results are refined and some functions now ask you to say what your columns are; see “Refined results” and “What works differently”.

New

  • Latency networks. build_network(method = "latency") builds a reply network in which faster replies carry more weight (Templeton et al. 2022).
  • Stability landscapes. stability_landscape() draws each state as a cup whose depth shows how long people stay in it. landscape_trend() follows the depths over time or along a covariate, and landscape_surface() draws them along a measure of stability.
  • Sequence patterns and indices. sequence_patterns() finds the patterns in sequences and tests them between groups. sequence_metrics() computes 23 indices for each sequence (entropy, turbulence, complexity, spells and others) and compares them between groups. pattern_outcome() relates patterns to an outcome, and extract_sequences() returns the sequences behind any input.
  • Phases. mark_phases() splits each person’s events into phases, so build_network(group = "phase") gives one network per phase.
  • Nested data. mosaic_test() tests counts nested in people or teams, and mosaic_plot() and mosaic_analysis() take nested and actor. permutation(), centrality_stability() and casedrop_reliability() take actor to resample whole people.
  • Entropy over time. entropy_trajectory() reads sequences as well as event logs, and its plot shows a bootstrap band around each trend.
  • Sequence plots by period. sequence_plot() can show actions per day, week or month (periods), and both sequence_plot() and distribution_plot() can drop rare columns (trim).
  • tna models can be passed wherever a network or sequences are accepted.
  • New dataset daily_actions: the learning actions of 30 students over seven days (simulated).
  • Smaller additions: node_clusters(), label_predictions() and label_scores(); nct() handles missing values and constant variables; extract_edges() and extract_initial_probs() read a group of networks; the build_*() shortcuts take group, scaling, threshold and params; build_mcml() reads edge lists; cooccurrence() and association_rules() read 0/1 tables (format = "binary"); compare_networks() marks significant differences in its difference plot; window_size in build_network(params = ) now works as in tna.

Refined results

These functions give refined results since 0.9.24.

  • nct() reported the structure test as the strength test and the other way round, and summary() swapped the in- and out-strength spreads.
  • build_mlvar() drew temporal edges in the wrong direction (from outcome to predictor).
  • sequence_compare() effect sizes changed with min_freq.
  • build_hypa() flagged anomalies in first-order data, which has none; it now uses a strength-preserving null. build_hon(method = "hon") now matches pyHON, and method = "hon+" missed some rules.
  • permutation() and compare_networks(test = "permutation") accepted two networks estimated in different ways (say Pearson and Spearman) and reported the difference as a difference between the groups. They now refuse.
  • boot_glasso(), build_mcml_pc() and loading_stability() ignored the network’s own estimator settings.
  • Numbers were corrected in centrality (BetweennessRSP, betweenness ties, min-max normalisation), net_prune(), build_mmm(), build_clusters(), build_mcml(), passage_time(), chain_structure(), markov_stability(), entropy_bayes(), hypergraph_centrality(), q_analysis(), persistent_homology(), betti_numbers(), bottleneck_distance(), pathways(), mogen_transitions(), extract_initial_probs(), mosaic_analysis(), predict_links() (ties), evaluate_links(), and the smoothing of landscape_surface() and landscape_trend().

What works differently

  • Say which column is which. Nestimate no longer guesses a column’s role from its name. Give action, actor and time for an event log, or state_cols for wide data, and format = "onehot" for 0/1 code columns. Extra columns in wide data (metadata, actor, time, order) are no longer read as states. Times must include a four-digit year.
  • Results are tables. These used to return lists or wide tables and now return one data frame, one row per item, with a group column when groups are compared: sequence_metrics(group = ), sequence_patterns(group = ), net_centrality() on several networks, and summary() of a grouped network, passage_time(), transition_entropy(), chain_structure(), markov_stability() and nct(). format = "wide" gives the old layout; table = picks the second table where there is one. Printing shows the first rows, summary() all of them.
  • Printing a network lists its strongest edges instead of the whole weight matrix.
  • New defaults. build_mogen() and markov_order_test() use dof = "paths" (dof = "observed" gives the old values). casedrop_reliability() compares only the edges a transition network has (target = "all" gives the old values), and it and centrality_stability() count a subset that fails as below the threshold.
  • Renamed. vertex_compare() columns are observed_x and observed_y; plot_state_frequencies(colors = ) is state_colors = (the old name still works, with a warning).
  • Refused inputs. Functions that read sequences refuse one-hot networks and association networks (correlation, partial correlation, glasso, Ising, mixed graphical models); resampling functions refuse a single sequence and networks built with level; latency networks can only be bootstrapped; Markov measures refuse correlation networks; entropy_trajectory() refuses missing times.
  • scaling = "normalize" on an undirected network returns a directed network when the rows no longer match the columns.
  • Arguments of sequence_plot() after group must be named.
  • prepare_onehot() and plot_mosaic() are no longer exported.
  • seed = no longer changes your session’s random numbers.

Documentation

  • “Comparing sequences between groups” is now an article on the package website instead of a vignette installed with the package; its address, PDF and DOI are unchanged.
  • Examples use 20 resamples (200 posterior draws) so they run quickly; a real analysis uses 1,000 or more.

Colours

Every figure colours states the same way: with no colours set, states get colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito colours in alphabetical order, and anything derived from a network keeps its colours. Plots that used rainbow, viridis or red-green now use these colours, with shapes or line types where colour alone separated groups.

Other fixes

  • plot() of entropy_trajectory() dropped groups with few windows.
  • plot() of bayes_compare() failed on a group of networks.
  • landscape_trend(along = ) failed on averaged metadata.
  • Colours set with set_state_colors() were lost after clustering.
  • subset() of compare_networks() tables printed only two decimals.
  • Data with a single state failed in bootstrap_network(), path_dependence() and predict_links().
  • labels = did not relabel the stored data.
  • sequence_plot() and distribution_plot() refused a data.table or tibble.
  • cluster_network() ignored its arguments.
  • The pyramid plot of sequence_compare() cut off its counts, and its printout now shows one row per pattern and group.

Nestimate 0.9.24

CRAN release: 2026-10-07

Documentation

  • Fixes to the 0.9.23 help-page merge, found in review:
    • Pages are named after their function again: build_mcml and plot_state_frequencies had been named after a print() method, and their usage now lists the function before its methods.
    • The descriptions of 51 methods (what a plot draws, what a print shows) are restored, as a “Methods” section on each function’s page.
    • Each page’s ... entry states what each method does with extra arguments: methods that reject them say so, plot.net_bayes() names cograph::splot(), and the rest say they are ignored.
    • compare_networks: the ... and labels entries no longer repeat; net_edge_betweenness and net_pruning_details no longer list a non-existent class.
    • Every S3 method has a documented return value.

Behaviour notes

  • The mgm estimator rejects scale = FALSE with a classed error (nestimate_mgm_unscaled); this started in 0.9.23 and was not listed there. Missing values are handled pairwise, now passed explicitly.

Tests

  • Two more reference-implementation tests (a hand-written linear solve for passage_time(), a manual multinom re-computation) and unused reference helpers moved to the local suite; section headers that claimed equivalence tests are renamed. New tests: mgm on data with missing values, and the scale = FALSE error.
